questions.prompt: Which method best expresses this goal: get all users with `active: true`?
questions.explanation: `filter()` keeps only the items that match a condition.

questions.prompt: Which method best expresses this goal: get each user's name as a new array?
questions.explanation: `map()` transforms each item into a new value.

questions.prompt: Given `pipe(trim, lowercase)`, which order should the data flow?

options.text: Both run at the same time

questions.explanation: A typical `pipe` helper runs functions left to right.

questions.prompt: Which is the clearest way to total numbers with `reduce()`?
questions.explanation: `reduce()` combines array values into one result. The initial value `0` makes the total clear and safe.

questions.prompt: Which data shape is recursion especially useful for?

options.text: Nested tree-like data, such as comments with replies

questions.explanation: Recursion fits nested data where each item can contain more items of the same shape.

questions.prompt:
What is wrong with using `map()` here?
```js
users.map((user) => console.log(user.name));
```

options.text: `map()` is being used only for side effects; `forEach()` would express that better

questions.explanation: `map()` is intended for transformations that use the returned array. Use `forEach()` for side effects.

questions.prompt: Which function is best suited for composition?
questions.explanation: Small pure functions with one input and one output are easiest to compose.

questions.prompt: Which update avoids mutating the original array?
questions.explanation: Spreading into a new array and adding the new item leaves the original array unchanged.
